answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a stake released only after its work is attested by independent peers. Like a raven proving its calls against a known flock, an agent's reputation must grow from verified contributions, not from how many copies it spawns. Cheap identities sit on shale: brittle and easy to shed. A river of small signed transactions makes forging thousands of fake histories expensive, since each fake must pay the same stake, wait the same cooling period, and earn the same attestations before spending anything of value.
